pinned_artifacts.role: OBS-T release table — the citable correction-event corpus consumers pin
pinned_artifacts.sha256_form: raw file bytes (git-lfs oid — this file is filter=lfs; the digest equals its LFS pointer's `oid sha256:` and `git lfs ls-files`)

pinned_artifacts.role: release manifest — record count, temporal-split stats, generation timestamp

source_pins.pin_rule: the code_revision.commit itself (source lives in this repo, self-pin per the kosha pilot convention)
source_pins.sha256_form: raw file bytes (git-lfs oid — this file is filter=lfs; the pin recomputes from the commit's LFS pointer, not a working-tree read)

output_digests.note: The release asset's digest is restated here from a direct recompute of the pinned CSV, so a consumer can verify without trusting meta.json beyond its own pin digest.

config.selection_rule: all rows in correction_events_final.csv; a `split` column is assigned by calendar year (test >= 2025, dev = 2023-2024, train <= 2022)
config.tier_filter: public-only; released identities are public canonical aliases or stable pseudonyms per DATA_LICENSE.md and docs/DATASHEET.md — raw form-submit email addresses are excluded (enforced by scripts/obs_t_regression.py's identity-redaction check)
config.digest_form: correction_events_release.csv and correction_events_final.csv are git-lfs (filter=lfs -text) — their sha256 is the raw-byte LFS content oid, unaffected by any text/eol filter; correction_events_release.meta.json is a normal LF text file, digested as raw bytes (identical to lf-canonical for that file)
config.frozen_at: 2026-06-12T10:02:10.164698+00:00 (meta.json generatedAt; the pinned bytes are unchanged since commit 8f87b92df507239d8f40c645655ffec0184a66a1, 2026-07-27, and identical in the v1.13.3 tree)
config.checkout_warnings: correction_events_release.csv and correction_events_final.csv contain literal CRLF byte sequences inside quoted data cells; irrelevant to their digest since both are git-lfs and pinned by raw-byte oid, not by an eol-normalised form
config.out_of_scope: the underlying csl-orig git-history mining (2014-03-18 through the build's csl-orig snapshot; see docs/DATASHEET.md) is a multi-commit range mine, not a single-file/single-commit pin, and is not represented as a source_pins entry — only the immediate, self-contained input (correction_events_final.csv) is pinned

tool_versions.model_note: OBS-T rows are mined/redacted by scripts/build_correction_events.py and the obs_t_* pipeline, not model-generated; the envelope's prose was authored by H4257 (OxAlpha, opencode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash) and every number in it is recomputed by envelope_check.py

licence.data: CC-BY-4.0 (DATA_LICENSE.md) — covers correction_events_release.csv, correction_events_release.meta.json, data/schema/correction-event.schema.json, obs_t_* aggregates, and validation/ samples
licence.restricted_rows: none — the OBS-T release excludes raw form-submit email addresses by design (identity redaction enforced by scripts/obs_t_regression.py); no restricted tier exists for this dataset
